messages:
ollie: deploybot reported a sudden p95 spike right after the staged rollforward in us-east1. safety valve paused at ~47%. reporting now.

deploybot: :warning: SAFETY-VALVE
metric=latency_p95 region=us-east1 duration=00:04 threshold=260ms current=380ms
suggested_action=reduce_traffic target_version=v3.0.0 cause=higher-latency-kernel

ria: oncall 1: looking at flame graphs: kernel selection for seqlen>1024 picks a fallback path that's slower. infra healthy. seems workload-dependent.

ollie: options: 1) auto_rollback full, 2) surgical slice rollback of the high-latency traffic slice, 3) keep paused and rollforward a kernel patch. prefer 2 to minimize churn.

sre-oncall: agree with surgical. identify slice ids with heavy long-sequence traffic then shift 25% away from v3.0.0. i'll prepare router change and lower autoscale for the new pool to avoid extra warmups.

ops_bot: INCIDENT LOGGED incident-6002 owners=ollie,ria severity=medium channel=#customer-facing-updates

ria: running router command to shift slice-42 25% back to v2.9.8 for us-east1 now:
```
routerctl traffic shift --slice slice-42 --from v3.0.0 --to v2.9.8 --percent 25 --region us-east1
```
Posting results in 2m.

ollie: i'll draft a short internal release note: "Partial traffic rollback in us-east1 due to latency regression affecting long-sequence workloads. Engineers investigating kernel selection; monitoring." cs_lead pls standby for customer notice.

cs_lead: on it. short message ready: "We detected increased latency for certain long-sequence requests after recent model rollout in us-east1. We have partially rolled back public traffic while we investigate. No dedicated customers impacted. Updates in 30m."

sre-oncall: router change applied. early metrics: p95 fell from 380ms -> 220ms within 3 minutes. KV-cache warm-up observed. no 5xx spike.

ria: confirming traces now look normal. the slow path is triggered by chunking logic; will open a kernel-flag PR to force preferred kernel for seqlen distribution. ETA for patch: T+4h.

ollie: keep monitoring for 30m. if stable, we'll keep the partial rollback and schedule the patch in next release. if it re-emerges, escalate to full rollback and customer comms. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
